title: WholeBodyWAM: Learning Whole-Body World Action Models with Scalable Motion Priors
abstract: Humanoid whole-body manipulation requires coordinated whole-body dynamics, yet large-scale trajectories from a target robot are expensive to collect and difficult to scale. In contrast, whole-body motion from human and humanoid sources is abundantly available, although such data cannot be directly used as embodiment-specific robot actions. This work asks whether these scalable motion resources can instead provide a transferable predictive prior for humanoid world-action modeling. We introduce WholeBodyWAM, a humanoid world-action model that learns whole-body dynamics from large-scale heterogeneous motion before target-robot training. We curate UniMotion-4K, a motion corpus spanning more than 4K hours from human videos, native 3D motion datasets, and heterogeneous humanoid platforms, and canonicalize these diverse sources into a unified motion space. A language-conditioned Motion Expert is then pretrained to predict future whole-body motion without target-robot action supervision. During robot post-training, the pretrained Motion Expert is integrated with Video and Action Experts through asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) attention, enabling predictive scene dynamics and whole-body motion to jointly inform embodiment-specific action generation. Experiments show that WholeBodyWAM consistently benefits from increased motion-pretraining scale, improves future-motion prediction and downstream task performance, and transfers effectively to real-world humanoid manipulation. Moreover, the pretrained motion prior substantially improves data efficiency under limited target-robot demonstrations.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: In our seminar on Embodied Foundation Models, we've discussed how systems like τ₀-WM are unifying video prediction and action generation. Today's lecture is on WHOLEBODYWAM: Learning Whole-Body World Action Models with Scalable Motion Priors, from a team at Nankai and Tsinghua University. This work tackles a similar goal but introduces a new twist. Instead of just predicting future pixels, it asks if we can also predict the robot's future body posture, and whether pretraining on massive human motion datasets can help. Yes, Noah?
segments.zh: 在我们关于具身基础模型的研讨课上，我们讨论过像τ₀-WM这样的系统是如何把视频预测和动作生成统一起来的。今天的讲座讲的是WHOLEBODYWAM：用可扩展的运动先验学习全身世界动作模型，来自南开和清华的团队。这项工作瞄准的目标类似，但带来了新的变化。它不只是预测未来的像素，而是问我们能不能同时预测机器人未来的身体姿态，以及在海量人体运动数据上做预训练能不能帮上忙。是的，Noah？

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hi Professor. So, if they're using human motion data, how is this different from the teleoperation or imitation learning systems we've seen, like TWIST?
segments.zh: 教授您好。那如果他们用的是人类动作数据，这跟我们之前看到的遥操作或模仿学习系统，比如TWIST，有什么区别呢？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That's the central question. The key difference is that they don't use the human motion to directly generate robot actions. Instead, they use it as a predictive signal to train a world model. The model learns to answer: 'Given this instruction and current state, what will my body's configuration look like in the near future?' This predicted future motion then serves as an intermediate guide for a separate action generation module. The core contribution is treating the robot's own body as a predictable part of the world state, right alongside environmental dynamics.
segments.zh: 这是核心问题。关键区别在于，他们不是用人类运动数据直接生成机器人动作，而是把它当作一个预测信号来训练世界模型。模型要学会回答：“给定这条指令和当前状态，我的身体构型在不久的将来会是什么样？”这个预测出的未来运动，再作为一个中间引导，提供给一个独立的动作生成模块。核心贡献在于，把机器人自己的身体当作世界状态中一个可预测的部分，和环境动态同等对待。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: That's an interesting framing. So the hypothesis is that a model that can anticipate its own posture is better at generating actions?
segments.zh: 这个角度挺有意思。所以假设就是，一个能预判自身姿态的模型，更擅长生成动作？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Precisely. The authors have three main objectives. First, to see if heterogeneous data—internet videos, mocap, other humanoid data—can provide useful supervision without needing action labels for their target robot, TianGong 3.0. This addresses the data bottleneck in humanoid robotics. Second, to build a shared motion representation to make this possible. They created a dataset called UniMotion-4K, with over 4,000 hours of motion data from 11 sources, all canonicalized into a common format. Third, they evaluate whether pretraining a model on this dataset actually improves the robot's performance, generalization, and data efficiency for downstream tasks.
segments.zh: 没错。作者有三个主要目标。第一，看看异构数据——互联网视频、动捕数据、其他人形机器人的数据——能不能在不需要目标机器人天工3.0动作标签的情况下提供有用的监督信号。这针对的是人形机器人领域的数据瓶颈问题。第二，构建一个共享的动作表示来让这件事成为可能。他们做了一个叫UniMotion-4K的数据集，包含来自11个来源、超过4000小时的动作数据，全部统一成一种通用格式。第三，他们评估在这个数据集上预训练模型，是否真的能提升机器人在下游任务上的表现、泛化能力和数据效率。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Wait, how do you create a 'common format' for motion across humans and different robots with completely different joints and body plans?
segments.zh: 等等，人类和不同机器人的关节和身体结构完全不同，你怎么给它们的动作建立一个“通用格式”呢？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Good question. They use a root-free, 63-dimensional representation. Each frame captures the local rotations for 21 key joints as axis-angle vectors. By removing global position and orientation, they focus purely on the articulated posture, which is more transferable across embodiments. For each specific robot, they train a small adapter—a simple MLP—that maps that robot's native joint states into this shared space. This allows them to pool data from humans, captured via vision models like GVHMR from videos, and other robots into one massive pretraining corpus.
segments.zh: 好问题。他们用了一种无根节点的63维表示。每一帧记录21个关键关节的局部旋转，用轴角向量表示。通过去掉全局位置和朝向，他们只关注关节姿态本身，这样在不同身体结构之间迁移起来更方便。对每个具体的机器人，他们会训练一个小型适配器——就是一个简单的MLP——把那个机器人原生的关节状态映射到这个共享空间里。这样一来，他们就能把人类的数据（通过GVHMR这类视觉模型从视频里提取的）和其他机器人的数据汇聚到一起，形成一个大规模的预训练语料库。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So that's the UniMotion-4K dataset. And how is it used in their training pipeline?
segments.zh: 这就是UniMotion-4K数据集。那它在他们的训练流程中是怎么用的呢？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The methodology is a two-stage process. In Stage I, they pretrain what they call a Motion Expert. This is a large transformer model conditioned on a language instruction. Its only job is to predict a sequence of future body motions in that shared 63D space, using flow matching to learn the dynamics. Importantly, this stage uses only the UniMotion-4K data; there are no target-robot actions or visual observations involved. It's purely about learning a general, task-conditioned prior over plausible human and humanoid body movements.
segments.zh: 这个方法分为两个阶段。在第一阶段，他们预训练了一个叫做运动专家的模型。这是一个以语言指令为条件的大型Transformer模型。它唯一的任务就是在那共享的63维空间中预测未来身体动作的序列，用流匹配来学习动力学。重要的是，这个阶段只用了UniMotion-4K数据，不涉及任何目标机器人的动作或视觉观测。它纯粹是在学习一个通用的、以任务为条件的先验，涵盖合理的人类和人形身体运动。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Okay, so it learns what 'kneeling' or 'picking something up' looks like in terms of abstract body posture. What happens in Stage II?
segments.zh: 所以它学的是“跪姿”或“捡东西”在抽象身体姿态上是什么样子。那第二阶段会发生什么？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: In Stage II, they take this pretrained Motion Expert and integrate it into a larger world-action model for their target robot, TianGong 3.0. This model has three components: the Motion Expert from Stage I, a Video Expert for predicting future visual scenes, and an Action Expert that generates the actual robot commands. These experts are interconnected using a Mixture-of-Transformers attention mechanism. The key here is the information flow: the Action Expert can attend to both the current visual input and the future motion predicted by the Motion Expert. So it can effectively ask, 'Given the scene and the goal of kneeling, what low-level motor commands should I execute?'
segments.zh: 在第二阶段，他们把这个预训练好的动作专家整合进一个更大的世界-动作模型里，用在目标机器人天工3.0上。这个模型有三个组件：第一阶段的动作专家、一个用来预测未来视觉场景的视频专家，还有一个生成实际机器人指令的动作专家。这些专家通过一种混合Transformer注意力机制互相连接。关键在于信息流动：动作专家既能关注当前的视觉输入，也能关注动作专家预测的未来动作。所以它实际上可以问：“给定这个场景和跪下的目标，我应该执行哪些底层的运动指令？”

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: And the predicted motion is never directly executed? It’s just an internal signal?
segments.zh: 那预测出来的动作从来不会直接执行吗？它只是一个内部信号？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Correct. It's a form of predictive supervision that guides the policy. It's not retargeted into commands. During deployment, the model predicts a 32-step chunk of executable actions. The upper-body commands are sent directly to the robot, while lower-body commands are handled by existing low-level controllers for balance and locomotion. This division of labor is a practical choice.
segments.zh: 没错，这是一种引导策略的预测性监督信号，并不会被重新转换成指令。部署时，模型会预测一段32步的可执行动作。上半身指令直接发送给机器人，下半身指令则由现有的底层控制器处理，负责平衡和行走。这种分工是一个务实的选择。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The results support this approach. WHOLEBODYWAM achieved an average task score of 72.2% across six manipulation and locomotion tasks, outperforming strong baselines like GR00T. The ablations are quite telling. Removing the motion pretraining dropped the score to 59.1%. And if they kept the pretraining but cut the information flow from the Motion Expert to the Action Expert, the score fell even further to 46.3%. This suggests both the learned prior and its integration are critical. This also echoes findings in other world models like EgoWAM, where auxiliary predictions can improve policy learning.
segments.zh: 结果支持了这种做法。WHOLEBODYWAM在六项操作和运动任务上平均任务得分达到72.2%，超过了GR00T等强基线。消融实验很能说明问题。去掉运动预训练后，得分降到59.1%。而如果保留预训练，但切断从运动专家到动作专家的信息流，得分进一步降到46.3%。这说明学到的先验和它的整合都很关键。这也和其他世界模型里的发现相呼应，比如EgoWAM，辅助预测能改进策略学习。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: A drop from 72% to 46% is significant. But what about the limitations? By using a root-free representation, aren't they throwing away crucial information about locomotion and global movement, which seems central to humanoid robotics?
segments.zh: 从72%掉到46%可不是小数目。但它的局限性呢？用这种无根表示，是不是把关于运动和全局移动的关键信息给扔掉了？而这些信息对人形机器人来说似乎至关重要。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That's an excellent point and a key limitation the authors acknowledge. The motion prior learns articulated posture changes but not the global dynamics of walking or balancing. That responsibility is offloaded to the robot's native action space and its low-level controllers. While this is a practical simplification, future work could explore integrating global dynamics into the shared representation. The other constraint is that human motion recovered from web video can be noisy. Still, the scaling experiments showed clear benefits: more pretraining data led to better performance, suggesting the model is robust to some level of noise.
segments.zh: 你说得很对，这也是作者承认的一个关键局限。这个运动先验学到的是关节姿态的变化，而不是行走或平衡的全局动力学。这部分责任被交给了机器人原生的动作空间和它的底层控制器。虽然这是一个实用的简化，但未来的工作可以探索把全局动力学整合进共享表示里。另一个限制是，从网络视频中恢复的人体运动可能带有噪声。不过，规模实验显示了明显的好处：更多的预训练数据带来了更好的性能，说明模型对一定程度的噪声是鲁棒的。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Ultimately, this paper's significance lies in its conceptual shift. It demonstrates that large-scale, action-free motion data can be a valuable source of predictive supervision for humanoid control. By modeling the robot's future body configuration as part of the world state, it provides a rich, intermediate signal that helps the policy reason about complex, whole-body tasks involving posture and balance.
segments.zh: 最终，这篇论文的意义在于它带来的概念转变。它证明了大规模、无动作的运动数据可以成为人形控制中预测性监督的宝贵来源。通过把机器人未来的身体构型建模为世界状态的一部分，它提供了一个丰富的中间信号，帮助策略对涉及姿态和平衡的复杂全身任务进行推理。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So the main takeaway is that for whole-body control, predicting what you're going to look like can be just as important as predicting what the world is going to look like.
segments.zh: 所以核心结论就是，对于全身控制来说，预测你自己接下来会变成什么样，可能和预测世界接下来会变成什么样同样重要。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Exactly. It reframes the problem from simple observation-to-action mapping to a more holistic prediction of the entire robot-environment system. Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 没错。这就把问题从简单的观察-动作映射，重新定义成了对整个机器人-环境系统的更全面的预测。感谢收听。如果还有任何问题，可以问我们的AI助手，或者留言评论。
